clue.text: Thief in Rheims and one in London abandoned by families

indicators.note: being abandoned by something means losing it, so that word drops out of the name

parts.note: Jack Dawkins, the Artful Dodger of Dickens's Oliver Twist, is a young thief working in London
kin means family, so families gives kins

explanation.surface: Two famous thieves, one French and one English, are compared, the latter left without any relations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jackdaw of Rheims is a ring-stealing bird in a comic poem from the Ingoldsby Legends. Dickens's Artful Dodger is Jack Dawkins; take KINS off his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ingoldsby Legends poem, a bird steals the cardinal's ring at Rheims, so the bird species names that thief.

clue.text: After end of May, this comes to each tree

annotationWithheld.clue: After end of May, this comes to each tree

clue.text: Tobacco has to be prearranged

definitions.meaning: a type of tobacco leaf that has been cut and cured

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally described herbs and tobacco ready for sale, and became idiom for something decided in advance.

clue.text: 17 become tedious

definitions.meaning: the answer to 17 down, a fierce bad-tempered old woman
to go on too long and become boring

explanation.walkthrough: 17 down is HARRIDAN, a fierce old woman, which is a figurative sense of the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fierce, overbearing woman; split in two, the phrase drag on means continue tediously.

clue.text: On friendly terms all the time? That surprises me!

parts.note: well in means on good terms with someone, in British idiom
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to learn two people have always been friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well in' is British slang for being on friendly terms with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a British idiom expressing astonishment, much like 'goodness me'.

clue.text: Millais's painting -— work he left in abeyance initially

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
taken as written

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the words in and abeyance

explanation.surface: An art critic describes Millais suspending work on a famous canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Millais's celebrated Pre-Raphaelite canvas shows Shakespeare's drowned heroine floating in a stream, and bears her name as its title.

clue.text: Left with eggs on the ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the eggs sit on top of the left

parts.note: ova are eggs, the plural of ovum

explanation.surface: Someone departs leaving eggs lying on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; 'the ground' looks like the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington, south London, is a famous Test cricket venue, so it is a ground.

clue.text: Pope: he is disciplined, used to water

indicators.note: disciplined means knocked into shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pope announces he has been punished, perhaps soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disciplined' makes an anagram of POPE HE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is a flexible tube that carries water to plants, so it is used for watering.

clue.text: Story needs to be buried

definitions.meaning: to be at rest in a grave, as in here rests

explanation.definitionFit: A fib is a falsehood, and the dead are said to rest in their graves, as on 'here lies' headstones.

clue.text: China to develop ancient city

indicators.note: develop means change and grow, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beijing intends to build up an old metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major city of the ancient Hellenistic and Roman world, in modern Turkey.

clue.text: Fan seen turning in 28

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters found are read backwards
something seen in a word is sitting inside it, so look for a short run of letters within the answer to 28
something seen in a word is sitting inside it, so look for a short run of letters within the answer to 28

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer of 28 across

explanation.surface: A supporter is spotted spinning round inside a domed hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 28 across is ROTUNDA; TUN sits inside it, and 'turning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is an informal word for an enthusiast or devotee, as in a golf nut.

clue.text: What you get after washday? Nothing conceded here

definitions.meaning: a freshly laundered bed linen item, playfully what laundry day produces
in football, a match in which a team lets in no goals

explanation.walkthrough: A clean sheet is a football term for a game in which the goalkeeper concedes no goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundered bedding is literally clean linen, while in sport the phrase is idiom for a game without conceding.

clue.text: Anteater scrambling on paling

indicators.note: scrambling means the letters are jumbled up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature that eats ants clambers hastily over a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambling' looks like climbing over the fence, but it signals an anagram of ON PALING.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaly mammal of Africa and Asia feeds on ants and termites, so it is an example of an anteater.

clue.text: God is Love: a survey heading

indicators.note: heading means going at the front, so the survey pieces lead and the zero follows

parts.note: taken as written
a poll is a survey of opinion
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: God is Love is presented as the headline of an opinion survey.
explanation.walkthrough: God Is Love reads as a religious slogan, but only 'God' is the definition; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman god of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Vent one's anger and fire second group of players

parts.note: to let off a gun is to fire it
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: An angry manager rants and sacks the reserve squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like sacking someone, but it means letting off a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting off steam is idiom for releasing pent-up feelings, from a boiler releasing pressure.

clue.text: Military unit in reserve

definitions.meaning: a group of troops sent away from the main force

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'reserve' means a cool, distant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached group of soldiers is a unit, and standing apart from others emotionally is also called this.

clue.text: Be carried by badger

definitions.meaning: to travel as a passenger on a horse or vehicle
as a verb, to pester or harass someone persistently

explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' here is the verb meaning to nag, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is travelling as a passenger; the other is the American idiom of riding someone, that is, needling them constantly.

clue.text: Tremendous excitement following almost every throw

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone gets very worked up after each throw in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the Y off EVERY to leave EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is an idiom for a state of extreme agitation or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Noisily pestered by an awful old woman

indicators.note: noisily means as spoken out loud, so a word is replaced by one that sounds like it

parts.note: harried means pestered

explanation.surface: Someone is loudly nagged by a dreadful old crone.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: in many accents the second syllable of the past participle is said with a weak vowel, so the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman.

clue.text: Subsequently appearing in court case involving several parties

indicators.note: appearing in signals that one word goes inside another

parts.note: a trial is a court case
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: A later court hearing turns out to involve multiple litigants.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilateral agreement is one between three sides, so it involves more than two parties.

clue.text: He performs feats that will hold water

definitions.meaning: an acrobat who does somersaults and flips
a drinking glass without a stem

explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat doing somersaults is called this, and so is a flat-bottomed drinking glass that contains liquid.

clue.text: Hairdo in the shape of a circle applied to a Father

indicators.note: applied to means attached after, so the circle comes after the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A priest has a round, bushy hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the shape of' just leads to the circle; 'applied to' puts O after A FR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded hairstyle of tightly curled hair.

clue.text: How butter may be spread with success

definitions.meaning: enjoying a run of good luck

explanation.definitionFit: Butter goes on a bread bun, and the phrase is also an idiom for a winning streak.

clue.text: Source from which Defoe's hero derived

indicators.note: derived means made from something else, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar traces the origin of a famous novelist's protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derived' makes an anagram of SOURCE; 'from which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson, the castaway of Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel, has this surname, so he is Defoe's hero.

clue.text: The way to get sailors up to date

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
RN is the Royal Navy, the British navy's sailors

explanation.surface: A guide explains how to keep naval personnel current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like a direction for the sailors, but it is part of the definition 'up to date'.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current, belonging to the present day, which is a synonym of up to date.

clue.text: Attraction of march is a beat

indicators.note: beat means battered or broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The appeal of a march lies in its rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' reads as the drumbeat of a march, but it signals an anagram of MARCH IS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, a compelling attractiveness or charm.

clue.text: Military commander imprisoning queen in Indian city

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A general jails a queen in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is a city in Uttar Pradesh, northern India.

clue.text: Direct a piercing glare

parts.note: a stare so hostile it is likened to throwing knives at someone

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means glaring at someone angrily, the eyes figuratively shooting knife blades.

clue.text: Means of escape not worth considering

definitions.meaning: a way ..., an exit or excuse

explanation.definitionFit: A way of escape is called this, and an idea that is ruled out is said to be this as well.

clue.text: I say nothing

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which can be signalled by say
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone declines to comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the definition: the self, as in one's own sense of identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the conscious 'I' of psychology.

clue.text: Listing covers German and Italian Pantheon, for instance

indicators.note: covers means goes round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a rota is a list of people's turns of duty
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A list includes German and Italian buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and Italian' looks like a pair, but 'German and' gives UND and 'Italian' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's Pantheon is a circular domed building, and such a round domed hall is an example of the architectural type.

clue.text: A lot of hot air about island —- discussion cut short

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: talk is discussion
Herm is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone talking pompously about an island has their discussion curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' takes the K off TALK, leaving TAL to go 'about' HERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising column of warm air, used by gliders and birds to gain height.
